recipes.name: Chai Po (Sweet Preserved Radish)
recipes.flavorProfile: Salty, sweet and chewy, with a crunch.
recipes.healthBenefit: Used by the spoonful for flavor; it is salty.

ingredients.cutPrep: peeled and cut in thick strips

ingredients.prepNote: 2 tbsp taken up by the radish, the rest drawn out with the water and squeezed away

instructions: Toss the radish with the salt and leave overnight under a weight. Squeeze out and pour away the liquid.
Dry in the sun or a 60 C (140 F) oven for 1 to 2 days, until leathery.
Toss with the sugar, pack into a jar and leave a week before using. Chop fine to use.

nutritionHighlights.note: High: about 1 g sodium per tablespoon.

recipes.name: Luk Chin Nuea (Thai Beef Balls)
recipes.flavorProfile: Springy, savory and peppery, with garlic and fish sauce.
recipes.healthBenefit: Lean beef brings protein, iron and zinc.
instructions: Grind the cold beef very fine in a food processor with the garlic, fish sauce, sugar, salt and pepper.
Add the starch, baking powder and ice water bit by bit and process until a sticky, smooth paste forms. Chill 1 hour.
Squeeze balls of about 15 g through your fist into warm water, then simmer gently 8 to 10 minutes until they float and spring back. Drain.

recipes.name: Kaep Moo (Pork Rinds)
recipes.flavorProfile: Puffed, crackly and salty, with a rich pork taste.
recipes.healthBenefit: Mostly protein from collagen and fat; a garnish rather than a main source of anything.

ingredients.prepNote: the fat the rind takes up in frying

instructions: Boil the rind for 30 minutes until soft, cool and scrape off the fat underneath. Cut into strips.
Dry in the sun or a 90 C (195 F) oven until hard, 6 to 8 hours.
Fry in hot lard at 200 C (390 F) a few at a time until they puff, drain well and toss with the salt. One serving is 20 g.

recipes.name: See Ew Dam Waan (Sweet Dark Soy Sauce)
recipes.flavorProfile: Thick, dark, sweet and salty, with a molasses edge.
recipes.healthBenefit: Used by the spoonful for colour and sweetness; it is high in sugar and salt.

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)
ingredients.prepNote: about 1 cup (250 ml); soy sauce weighs about 1.08 g per ml
stands in for Thai palm sugar, which no food database here lists

instructions: Melt the sugar in the water over low heat, then stir in the molasses and soy sauce.
Simmer gently, stirring, for 10 to 15 minutes until it coats a spoon thickly. It thickens more as it cools.
Cool and keep in a clean jar in the fridge. It makes about 600 g.
recipes.curationNote: Thai sweet dark soy is soy sauce cooked with molasses and sugar. One serving is one tablespoon, about 18 g, from a finished weight of about 600 g.

recipes.name: Sriracha (Fermented Chilli Sauce)
recipes.flavorProfile: Hot, garlicky, tangy and a little sweet.
recipes.healthBenefit: Fresh chillies bring vitamin C; used by the spoonful.
instructions: Blend the chillies, garlic, sugar and salt to a coarse paste. Pack into a jar, cover loosely and leave at room temperature for 3 to 5 days, stirring daily, until it smells sour and bubbles.
Blend with the vinegar until smooth, then simmer 5 minutes.
Push through a sieve if you want it smooth, cool and keep in the fridge. It makes about 600 g.

nutritionHighlights.note: Fresh red chillies are rich in vitamin C, though some is lost in cooking.

recipes.curationNote: One serving is one tablespoon, about 17 g, from a finished weight of about 600 g.

recipes.name: Kratiam Dong (Thai Pickled Garlic)
recipes.healthBenefit: Garlic, softened by pickling; eaten a few cloves at a time.

ingredients.cutPrep: small whole heads, outer skin rubbed off

ingredients.prepNote: the share taken up by the garlic; the jar holds 250 ml
the share taken up; the brine holds 100 g
the share taken up; the brine holds 15 g

instructions: Soak the garlic heads in salted water overnight, drain and pack into a clean jar.
Boil 250 ml rice vinegar, 250 ml water, 100 g sugar and 15 g salt, cool and pour over the garlic.
Close and leave 3 to 4 weeks before using. Only about a quarter of the brine is eaten with the garlic, so only that share is counted.

nutritionHighlights.note: Pickling mellows the sharp sulfur compounds of raw garlic.

recipes.curationNote: The brine water is left out because it is not eaten. One serving is one tablespoon of cloves, about 20 g, from about 500 g of pickled garlic.

recipes.name: Pla Ra (Fermented Fish)
recipes.flavorProfile: Very salty, pungent and deeply savoury.
recipes.healthBenefit: A seasoning used by the spoonful; it is very salty.

ingredients.cutPrep: small freshwater fish, scaled, gutted and cleaned
ingredients.prepNote: stands in for the mud carp and gourami used in Isan

instructions: Mix the cleaned fish with the salt and leave overnight in a covered jar.
Mix in the roasted rice bran, pack tightly into a clay or glass jar, seal and leave in a cool place for at least 6 months, up to a year.
For pla ra sauce, simmer fish and liquid with a little water and strain. It makes about 1.2 kg.

nutritionHighlights.note: Very high: about 1.4 g sodium per tablespoon.

recipes.curationNote: Isan pla ra uses small freshwater fish, salt and roasted rice bran or roasted rice. One serving is one tablespoon, about 18 g.

recipes.name: Pu Dong (Salted Field Crab)
recipes.flavorProfile: Salty and briny, with a strong crab taste.
recipes.healthBenefit: Small amounts season som tam; it is salty.

ingredients.prepNote: the share taken up; the brine holds 100 g in 1 litre of water

instructions: Scrub the crabs well and rinse in several changes of water.
Boil 1 litre of water with 100 g salt, cool completely and pour over the crabs in a jar. Close and leave 2 to 3 days in the fridge.
Crush a crab or two into the mortar for som tam. The brine is not eaten, so only the salt the crabs take up is counted.
recipes.curationNote: Field crabs carry parasites when eaten raw; brining does not kill them, so many cooks now steam the crabs before salting. One serving is one crab, about 25 g.
